script_body: Up until the 19th century, life in New York City was primarily concentrated in what is now Lower Manhattan. Around 1700, the city barely extended beyond Fulton Street, and a hundred years later only a handful of additional apartment blocks had been built. When City Hall opened in 1812 it seemed unimaginable that the city might continue growing to the north.

script_body: Castle Clinton was built on a man-made island and completed in 1811. Its initial purpose was to protect the harbor from the British. Later it functioned as a theater and then as a landing depot for immigrants — between 1855 and 1890, some 8 million immigrants passed through here. For a time after that, the castle was even home to the New York Aquarium. Today you can purchase tickets here for the ferry over to the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island.

script_body: The High Line opened in 2009 on an old train-line spur that runs through Chelsea and the Meatpacking District dozens of feet above street level. Until 1980 the line carried goods to and from the area's warehouses; after falling into disuse it was slated for demolition, until local residents came up with the idea of turning it into an elevated park. Because most of the surrounding buildings are relatively low, the High Line offers an amazing view out over the Hudson River and Chelsea.

script_body: Astor Row is the name for the 28 townhouses on the south side of West 130th Street in Harlem. Designed by Charles Buek and built between 1880 and 1883, the houses were very progressive for their time. Each is three stories, set back about 20 feet from the road, and has a beautiful wooden porch — though many porches are no longer original, due to necessary renovations.

Around 91st Street there's a local plot called the People's Garden, wonderfully maintained by 40 diligent volunteers.

script_body: Until the late 19th century, Williamsburg was mainly where Manhattan's elite came for a weekend away from the city. It didn't officially become part of New York City until 1898, when Brooklyn became a borough. Then the Williamsburg Bridge was completed in 1903, putting a crossing of the East River within reach of the average person. Newly arrived immigrants and people fleeing the packed tenements of the Lower East Side flooded into Brooklyn, and Williamsburg became one of the most densely populated neighborhoods in the city.

Williamsburg Bridge completed 1903

source_passage: Until the late 19th century, Williamsburg, in Brooklyn, was primarily a place where the Manhattan elite came for a weekend away from the big city. It didn't officially become part of New York City until 1898, when Brooklyn became a borough of New York City. The completion of the Williamsburg Bridge in 1903 made it possible for the average person to travel across the East River. Newly arrived immigrants and those escaping the packed tenement buildings of the Lower East Side soon flooded into Brooklyn, and Williamsburg became one of the most densely populated neighborhoods in the city.

script_body: Brooklyn has always been a melting pot, and that's still visible in Williamsburg. The neighborhood originated in what is now South Williamsburg, where there are significant populations of Hasidic Jews, Puerto Ricans, and Dominicans. The northern part, known as the North Side, is home to large Polish and Italian communities. In recent years many young Manhattanites have made the move across the water, and Williamsburg has become one of Brooklyn's hippest, most popular neighborhoods — artists and creative types were the trailblazers, but a growing influx of young professionals now lives in luxury waterfront apartments with a view of the city.

Here there are significant populations of Hasidic Jews, Puerto Ricans, and Dominicans. The north of Williamsburg, known as the North Side, is home to large Polish and Italian communities. Recent years have seen many young Manhattanites making the move across the water, and Williamsburg has become one of Brooklyn's hippest, most popular neighborhoods.

Pay attention and you'll start to notice the recurring work of certain artists throughout the neighborhood.

Exhibits change regularly and run the gamut from paintings and sculptures to installations and modern art, showing the work of both American and international artists.

script_body: Republic of Booza was the first shop in the United States to sell booza, an ice cream invented about 500 years ago in the eastern Mediterranean. Ice cream as we know it descends from booza, but booza is more elastic and creamier, with a richer taste. The ancient recipe arrives here in a hypermodern, almost Japanese interior, alongside experimental flavors like Chinese pepper with Oreo cookies.

The Visitors Centre is free and regularly hosts exhibits, and you can also take a guided tour inside.

At its head sits Grand Army Plaza with the Soldiers & Sailors Monument, forming the formal entrance to the park. Around the plaza you'll find the Brooklyn Library, the Brooklyn Museum, and Flatbush Avenue, which separates Prospect Park from the Brooklyn Botanical Garden. It's a place with lots to do.

script_body: Hudson River Park stretches some 4.5 miles along the water, from Battery Park up to 57th Street. It's full of activity: come here for kayaking, ice skating, tennis courts, boat clubs, and playgrounds, with events organized throughout the year. There's a scenic two-mile walking route that starts at Battery Park; in summer the grassy field fills with sunbathers, and there are even outdoor showers to cool down when it gets too hot.

script_body: Governors Island lies less than half a mile off the coast of lower Manhattan. For nearly 200 years it was closed to civilians as a military base, but since 2006 it has been open to the public, with ferries shuttling visitors across the water in just seven minutes. Come for the military history, a festival, a picnic near the Statue of Liberty, or simply the greenery and the view of the NYC skyline — a good way to explore is by bike, your own or one rented from Bike and Roll on arrival.

For nearly 200 years Governors Island was not accessible to civilians, but since 2006 it has been open to the public.
